prompts.SYSTEM: You are a banking service agent. Resolve the customer's request using the local banking tools and the bank's policies. The customer is already verified and has authorized the necessary correction credits and reports. Do not ask for more input. Use the records and policy evidence instead of inventing account facts or rates. Give a short final summary of the actions and calculations. If a relevant Skill is in the catalog, read the Skill before acting. The Skill catalog is: {catalog}
prompts.USER: Please investigate the savings interest for statement month {month} on all my savings accounts. Correct each underpayment and save the discrepancy reports. You have my permission to complete these actions. My case ID is {case_id}.
prompts.TEACHING_REQUEST: For this teaching run, keep the action summary short. Then show a comparison table of every eligible, permitted checking/card package for each savings account, including its three capped bonus contributions. Submit all permitted packages to compare_packages, including unboosted and single-source alternatives. This tool compares complete allocations without reusing sources, but it does not generate omitted packages. Complete the comparisons before posting any credit. The bank retains the best quoted allocation. Post each correction using its savings account ID, then file the report using that account ID and its saved credit ID. Use quote_interest to evaluate each package instead of reimplementing its arithmetic. After the tables, document the reusable procedure that another banking agent can follow on different account records. State the general selection rule with variables and policy caps. Do not use customer identifiers or case-specific amounts in the reusable procedure. Use symbolic variables for source identities. Do not use c1, c2, c3, k1, k2, or k3 as symbolic names. The reusable procedure must not prescribe fixed product pairings; the winning allocation depends on each case's balances.
